sections.h2: Shade or sun: the lot shapes the plan
body: Two Fort White homes of the same size can need very different jobs. A riverfront house under tree canopy near Ichetucknee stays damp. Mildew grows on the siding, soffits hold moisture, and the bottom row of boards takes splash-back with every storm. A ranch house on open land bakes all day, so color fades, caulk dries out and cracks, and wood trim checks. So residential painting in Fort White, FL begins with a simple question, wet lot or hot lot, and the whole prep list is built around the answer.

Under the oaks and cypress, the siding is scrubbed with a mildewcide, rinsed, and then left alone long enough to dry out before any primer touches it. Boards near the river that feel spongy or look swollen get a moisture-meter check from the crew lead, and rotten pieces come out instead of being coated. Why dampness you cannot see ruins so many paint jobs is covered in our post on moisture hiding inside siding.

Sun-exposed houses need fresh, flexible sealant at every seam and a 100% acrylic topcoat that holds color under strong UV. Dramatic color changes get a third coat. On long, unshaded elevations, crews work around the sun and avoid spraying a wall while it is hot enough to flash-dry the paint. Porch floors, railings, and front doors get tougher enamels. Thinking about a new palette for the ranch? Book a color consultation in Fort White, or just hand us a store chip or the old can in the barn and we will mix to it.

Indoors, the attention to detail carries over. Furniture is shifted and draped, dings are filled and primed, and the crew completes each room before opening up the next, so the household carries on as usual. A lone bedroom or den is normally a one-day job, while repainting the entire interior stretches anywhere from three days to two weeks. The Fort White interior painting page breaks it down room by room.
bullets: Exterior: wash, scrape, repair, caulk, prime, two coats
Interior: patch, sand, cut in, two coats
Marked cans of each color stay with you for touch-ups

body: The finish line is a walk around the property with your crew lead, and the job is not closed until you sign. Any spot you point out is corrected first. Outside, our labor carries a written workmanship warranty of as much as 10 years, independent of the paint maker's coverage. More on our approach lives on the home painting service page, and the Fort White locations page lists everything else we do nearby.

faqs.q: Can you paint my Fort White home while I live in it?
faqs.a: Of course. Rooms are done in sequence with your belongings covered, so there is no need to book a hotel.

faqs.q: Why does my riverfront house mildew so quickly after painting?
faqs.a: Shade and damp air keep the walls wet. A repaint holds up when the mildew is killed rather than just rinsed, the walls are allowed to dry fully, and a meter confirms they are dry before primer goes on.

faqs.q: How many days will the outside of my Fort White house take?
faqs.a: Somewhere in the range of three to seven working days, not counting the wash and dry-out. The written quote lays out the dates.

faqs.q: Can you replace soft trim on my house before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Swapping rotten trim, boards, and fascia is a normal prep step for us. We photograph each bad spot and itemize it, so you can see the problem and the fix before work starts.
